summary: Math.asinh is implemented per the spec steps. Step 1 calls ops::to_number(agent, x)? with the abrupt completion propagated. Step 2 returns n unchanged when it is not finite (NaN, ±Infinity) or equal to 0.0; in Rust, -0.0 == 0.0 is true, so both zeros are covered. Step 3 returns Value::Number(n.asinh()) for finite nonzero input. No special-cased inputs, no swallowed errors, no unrelated edits. The only cosmetic issue is that the step comments appear twice (the original block above the code is kept and repeated per line), which does not affect behaviour.
